The Responses dialect sends the system prompt as instructions, not as an input message

A ChatGPT plan credential at api.openai.com refused every request of session
20261007T152356Z-a337f2a9 (gpt-6.1-sol, dialect "responses") with 400
{"detail":"System messages are not allowed"}: both turns failed on their first
request, in milliseconds, with no model call made. toResponses put the system
prompt in input with role "system". It is now the request's top-level
instructions, for every credential; any further system messages are joined in
order, so none is dropped.

The fake Responses servers (test/fakes/chat and the one in internal/llm) now
refuse a system input item in that server's {"detail": ...} shape and accept
here (make validate, 0 warnings). make accept failed once on
not use the dialect); it passed alone and in the full internal/core package
twice, and in the second make validate.

Not shown: that the plan server accepts the request as sent. Nothing here talks
to OpenAI, and a field it refuses next would show on the first real turn.
